key_insight: A conductive GaOx hole transport layer can be formed by ion exchange during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling high-voltage 1.0 eV bottom cells without added Ag or heavy alkalis.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for tandem-ready chalcopyrite bottom cells, helping push CuInSe2 devices above 16% efficiency with VOC over 550 mV.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap CuInSe2 absorber via ion exchange.
Tested whether added Cu, Na, and sputtering oxygen flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Characterized the oxide as partly crystalline and evaluated device performance in a solar cell stack.
evidence_signal: The optimized stack achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV in a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx behavior appears process-dependent and partly crystalline, so maintaining reproducibility across fabrication conditions may be challenging.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
